spec.description: Autonomous behavior transparency: decision-path mix, self-healing by source, autotune calibration, Ollama run stats, containment releases, scheduled-job health. Prometheus-only.

options.content:
**Is the system actually getting smarter, and can I trust what it does while I'm not watching?**

This dashboard is Prometheus-only by design -- every panel here works even if Loki is never wired up (see System Health's own note on that). It covers four things the other dashboards don't: which reasoning path resolved each decision and whether that mix is improving over time, how much self-healing is autonomous vs a human tap, whether the autotune self-calibration system is adjusting itself safely, and whether every scheduled background job actually ran when it was supposed to.

spec.title: 🧭 Brain 1 / HEE: Decision-Path Mix Over Time
spec.description: Which branch of decision_engine.py's decision order actually resolved each evaluation (hard_stop/tier5_confirmed/hypothesis_high/hypothesis_suspicious/tier4_unconfirmed/ml_anomaly/benign). This is the direct 'is the system getting smarter over time' signal: watch the hard_stop/tier5 share shrink and the benign share grow across weeks as autotune calibration, CL-AFPE's trust cache, and the CDN/vendor allowlist absorb more of what used to need a hard corroborated signal to resolve correctly.

spec.title: 🧭 Decision-Path Share (Last 24h)
spec.description: Same data as the timeseries to the left, collapsed to one 24h window -- the proportions are the headline number; use the timeseries to spot exactly when the mix shifted.

spec.title: 🛡️ Self-Healing: Domains Immunized by Source
spec.description: fp_engine_domains_immunized_total split by source (autonomous = CL-AFPE's own Stage 2/3 suppress path, operator = a Telegram 'Mark False Positive' tap, llm_validated = Ollama's autonomous 4-hourly validation pass). The whole point of this session's self-calibration work was to make 'autonomous' and 'llm_validated' the dominant sources over time, not 'operator' -- a human shouldn't need to keep pace with every alert for the system to keep healing itself.

spec.title: 🛡️ Self-Healing: Sensitivity Adjustments by Source
spec.description: fp_engine_sigma_shifts_total split the same way -- every TUNE_DOWN (a confirmed false positive widening a device's baseline) or TUNE_UP (a confirmed threat tightening it) event, attributed to what triggered it.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Global Suppress Threshold — Effective vs Baseline
spec.description: The single most direct 'is the system healing itself' chart: the live effective fp_combined_suppress_threshold (green, from state/config_overrides.json if calibration has acted, else identical to baseline) against your own hand-set config.yaml baseline (the two lines start identical; effective should trend at or below baseline over time, never above -- calibration is one-directional by design and never raises it).

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Calibration Pass Outcomes (Cumulative)
spec.description: Every calibration pass classified by outcome: applied (threshold actually lowered), refused_ambiguous (an uncorrected UNCERTAIN alert overlapped the confirmed-FP range -- refused to auto-resolve that), insufficient_samples (not enough pooled corrections yet), no_change_needed (evidence didn't support going any lower than the current value). Refusals are as informative as applications here -- they're proof the system isn't blindly loosening just because it can.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Per-Device Calibrated Thresholds
spec.description: Devices that have earned their own calibrated suppress threshold (>=3 pooled corrections of that specific device's own evidence) -- devices not listed here still use the global effective value. A strongly different profile (e.g. a chatty IoT device) converges on its own number here rather than forcing one global threshold onto every device.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Evidence Samples Pooled (Global)
spec.description: How close the global pass is to its next calibration decision: corrected = confirmed false positives pooled since the last write (needs >=5 to act), uncorrected = never-corrected UNCERTAIN alerts in the same window (any overlap with the corrected range blocks calibration entirely, regardless of count).

spec.title: 🕵️ Ollama: Time Since Last Successful Run
spec.description: Scheduled every 4 hours by scripts/scheduler.py. Should never exceed roughly 4-5h under normal operation -- a much larger number here means the job silently stopped firing (exactly the class of bug a job-key/filename mismatch caused once already in this project) without anyone noticing until they went looking.

spec.title: 🕵️ Ollama: Calls / Cache Hits / Deferred (Last Run)
spec.description: A single noisy pattern that fired 50 times only ever costs one Ollama call, reused from the 7-day cache on every subsequent run it keeps recurring -- this is the direct evidence that 'call Ollama sparingly' is actually happening, not just a log claim. Deferred > 0 means the per-run cap was hit; those patterns retry next run, prioritized by which repeated most.

spec.title: 🕵️ Ollama: Cumulative Validated Verdicts
spec.description: Every LLM classification that passed DeterministicValidator's hallucination guardrail, since state/ollama_run_stats.json existed, split benign vs malicious. This is a running total, not a per-run count -- the trend across weeks is what matters.

spec.title: 🔓 Pi-hole Unblocks by Reason
spec.description: 'immunized' = an autonomous or operator correction released a block that was no longer warranted (the core of 'block only what's absolutely necessary'). 'manual' = an explicit operator release via the Grafana IPC endpoint or a device-level release. This is the release-side counterpart to the block-side 'Lifetime Threats Blocked' panel on the Main Overview dashboard -- until this session neither existed.

spec.title: 🔓 Router Isolation Releases by Reason
spec.description: 'device_marked_safe' = automatic release once a device is confirmed safe (safe_ips/patterns). 'manual' = an explicit operator release via Telegram or Grafana. Router isolation is deliberately latched -- it is never auto-released purely because traffic decayed to zero -- so every release here is a real, attributable decision, not a timeout.

spec.title: 📅 Scheduled-Job Health
spec.description: Time since each scheduled job's last successful completion, and how long that run took. Directly targets the exact class of bug already found once in this project -- a job-key/filename mismatch that silently never ran, with nothing surfacing the failure beyond a daemon log line nobody was watching. Expected staleness: ollama_soc ~4h, retro_hunter/top_domains_report/train_fp_classifier ~24h.

spec.title: 📅 Retro-Hunt Findings (Cumulative)
spec.description: Total retroactive threat-intel matches found by retro_hunter.py since state/job_health.json existed -- domains your network talked to that were unknown-clean at the time but have since been classified malicious by fresh OSINT.
